To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the substitution of repurchases for dividends is a recent development, and (ii) firms that have repurchased shares have financed their repurchases by reducing their dividends or by not increasing them as much as they would have otherwise.

(1) repurchases are becoming an important form of cash payout for U.S firms; (2) firms finance their share purchases with funds that otherwise they would have used to increase their dividends; (3) younger firms and large firms are more likely to repurchase shares than to increase dividends; and (4) the substitution of repurchases for dividends is a gradual process.
